summary: Eun-young Choi is a scholar in Buddhist studies who earned a doctorate at Korea University. She held a post as an HK Professor at Geumgang University, attested between 2013 and 2015.

Eva K. Neumaier works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, having studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Rigzin. She held posts at the University of Calgary (including Numata Professor, attested 2006) and the University of Alberta as Professor Emeritus and department chair.

Eva Tichy is an indologist and linguist who earned her Dr. phil. under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg and completed her Habilitation at the University of Marburg. From 1993 to 2017, she held the Lehrstuhl für Indogermanistik at Freiburg.

Eva Wilden is an indologist who completed her MA, doctorate, and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She served as Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient in 2003 and became a professor at the University of Hamburg in 2017.

Evan Thompson works in philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Amherst College and the University of Toronto under teachers including Robert A. F. Thurman and Francisco J. Varela, he has held professorships at Toronto (~2005–2013) and the University of British Columbia (2013).

Evgenij Ivanovich Kychanov worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at the Faculty of Oriental Studies of St. Petersburg University, he served as head of the St. Petersburg branch of the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts in 2002.

Eviatar Shulman works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1999–2008), where he became Chairman of comparative religion in 2009 and is attested as Professor in 2026.

Eyal Aviv is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under doctoral supervisors Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, and held a post at George Washington University in 2014.

F. B. J. Kuiper was an indologist and linguist who studied at Utrecht and Leiden universities under teachers including Willem Caland. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Leiden University (1939–1972) and directed the Kern Institute (~1946–1977).

Fa Qing is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a dissertation at the University of Calgary under doctoral supervisor Leslie S. Kawamura, interim supervisor A. W. Barber, and teacher Xiaojie Yang.

Fabienne Jagou works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. She completed her PhD at the School for Advanced Studies in the Social Sciences under Pierre-Étienne Will (~1994–1999) and was appointed Maître de conférences at the École française d'Extrême-Orient around 2001.

Fabio Rambelli specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Educated at Ca' Foscari, Naples "L'Orientale", and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies, he taught at Sapporo University (2001–2002) before becoming Shinto Studies Chair and Distinguished Professor at UC Santa Barbara (~2009).

Fabrizia Baldissera is an indologist who studied at the Department of Mathematics "Federigo Enriques" (1969–2004). She held academic posts at the University of Florence (~1998) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale".
Fafang was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He held a position as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-Kuei Li was a linguist, sinologist, and tibetologist who earned his PhD at Chicago under Edward Sapir. He held major appointments at Academia Sinica (1929, 1973), the University of Washington (1949–1969), and the University of Hawaiʻi (1969–1974).
Faren is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008. In 2013, Faren is attested as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong.

Farzand Ali Durrani was a historian and archaeologist who studied at the University of the Punjab, the University of Peshawar, and the University of London. He served as a professor at the University of Peshawar from approximately 1976 to 1993.

Fawad Khan is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a master's at the University of Peshawar and a PhD at Quaid-i-Azam University. In 2022, he was attested as Assistant Curator at the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Directorate of Archaeology and Museums.

Fazun was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Taixu, Amdo Geshe, and Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, among others. He directed the Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Institute (1933) and served as vice president and president of the Buddhist Academy of China (1956).

Feng Youlan was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Peking and Columbia universities. He held a long-term post at Tsinghua University (~1928–1952) and visiting appointments at the University of Pennsylvania and the University of Hawaiʻi (~1946–1947).
